coach_notes.note: Roee's easy/shakeout runs consistently show well-controlled HR (mid-130s-145s) relative to effort, and his aerobic hill-day HR staying lower than his flat volume-run HR suggests hills are his relative strength — a durable aerobic profile pattern worth tracking rather than a one-off.

His weight training sessions consistently run as low-cardiovascular-strain work (avg HR in the 80s) that slots cleanly around his running load without adding to fatigue, making strength days a reliable low-risk placeholder even when running-driven fatigue (TSB) is deeply negative.

In fartlek/surge-float sessions, Roee tends to hold prescribed paces well but lets HR drift progressively upward rep-to-rep (surges creeping toward max HR, floats failing to drop back into target range), indicating a pattern of pacing discipline without matching intensity discipline.

Roee has a consistent pattern of running "easy"/recovery-labeled sessions at moderate effort (pace and HR both drifting above prescribed ceilings after the first 2-3km), suggesting he struggles to genuinely back off intensity on designated easy days even when explicitly warned in advance.

Roee's weight-training sessions are the one part of his training he reliably keeps low-intensity, but he uses them (and other easy-labeled sessions) as an excuse to avoid taking genuine full rest days, letting rest-day debt accumulate even when each individual session looks fine.
